Disney earnings beat estimates as Bank of America raises price target to $135

Walt Disney Co (NYSE:DIS, XETRA:WDP) delivered stronger-than-expected quarterly results across its businesses, prompting Bank of America (BofA) to raise its price target and reaffirm its 'buy' rating on the entertainment group.

Revenue for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 increased 16% to $25.9 billion, exceeding the brokerage's $24.7 billion estimate, while operating income rose 43% to $5 billion against its $4.9 billion forecast.

Adjusted earnings per share of $1.77 also beat the bank's estimate of $1.70, reflecting strength across Disney's portfolio.

The brokerage described near-term investment in streaming as prudent given the longer-term growth opportunity, noting that Disney expects to deliver $3 billion in cost reductions by fiscal 2029, with much of the savings directed towards funding streaming operations.

Disney expects double-digit adjusted earnings per share growth in fiscal 2027, excluding the impact of an additional 53rd week, with total segment operating income forecast to increase about 8%.

The company expects high-single-digit operating income growth in its Experiences and Entertainment divisions, while Sports is projected to deliver double-digit growth.

However, growth across the businesses will be uneven, with Entertainment gains concentrated in the first quarter and Experiences expected to remain broadly flat in the second half.

Disney also forecast about $11 billion in free cash flow and $9 billion in share repurchases for fiscal 2027, while increasing its dividend by 33%.

Learn more about Walt Disney

Read more about Walt Disney

BofA lowered its fiscal 2027 operating income estimate to $20.4 billion from $20.8 billion following changes to segment reporting, but raised its adjusted earnings per share forecast to $7.60 from $7.52.

The brokerage increased its price target to $135 from $125, citing improving streaming profitability, renewed growth at theme parks, opportunities at ESPN and a strengthened senior management team.

title: Home Depot sales momentum strengthens as Bank of America sees scope for share gains
detail:
Home Depot sales momentum strengthens as Bank of America sees scope for share gains

BAC

HDI
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Home Depot Inc (NYSE:HD, XETRA:HDI) is well positioned to accelerate market share gains as sales momentum improves, Bank of America said, maintaining its 'buy' rating on the home improvement retailer.

The brokerage said third-quarter comparable sales were positive in 13 of the company's 16 merchandise categories, led by strength in power tools, storage, plumbing and electrical products.

Its Pro business continued to outperform, while do-it-yourself sales returned to positive comparable growth for the first time since the third quarter of 2025.

Sales of big-ticket items also accelerated, with comparable sales rising 4.5%, providing further evidence of improving demand.

The bank modestly raised its fiscal 2026 earnings per share estimate by $0.03 to $14.98, reflecting the third-quarter results, while maintaining its fiscal 2027 forecast of $15.55.

The fiscal 2027 estimate assumes comparable sales growth of 2.2% and flat operating margins, with pressure expected in the first half before improvement in the second half.

The brokerage expects Home Depot to consider price increases in selected categories and pursue cost savings to offset supply-chain disruption and broader cost pressures.

Learn more about Home Depot

Read more about Home Depot

Management has lowered its fourth-quarter gross margin expectations because of product mix and the impact of recent HVAC acquisitions, while promotional activity remains controlled and below last year's level.

The company also reduced its full-year revenue outlook for its SRS distribution business, which serves professional contractors, to low-single-digit organic growth from mid-single-digit growth, reflecting weakness in roofing demand.

However, SRS continued to deliver positive comparable sales, and Home Depot reported market-share gains in landscaping, pools, interiors and HVAC.

BoA expects share repurchases to resume once the company reaches its debt leverage target next year.

This article first appeared on GuruFocus.

Betting on semiconductor stocks is still the market's most crowded trade, according to Bank of America's November Global Fund Manager Survey.

But only 39% of respondents put it at the top, down from 82% in July. The trade has held its No. 1 ranking even as the share of managers who see it as the most crowded has more than halved.

The next closest trades were betting against Chinese equities, cited by 14% of respondents, and betting on the Magnificent Seven, at 12%. The survey ran from Nov. 6 to 12 and covered 193 panelists managing $526 billion.

The survey also found that managers made their biggest cut to technology overweights since 2006. Meanwhile, 52% expect a major cloud provider to announce a capital spending cut within six months, up from 30% in October.

An AI bubble was the most frequently cited market tail risk, at 34%, followed by a credit event at a major cloud provider, at 31%.

Investors Takeaway

The drop from 82% to 39% measures how managers rank the trade's crowding. The survey's technology allocation figures show that managers reduced exposure to the broader sector, while the size of any pullback from chip stocks specifically remains unclear.

The next test is what cloud providers say about their spending plans. A cut could weaken expectations for future chip orders while semiconductors still top the crowding rankings.

title: Banks Enhance Digital Debit Card Management, Money Movement and Accessibility for Online Banking
detail:

Banks Enhance Digital Debit Card Management, Money Movement and Accessibility for Online Banking
PR Newswire

BAC
Trade BAC on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Bank of America and U.S. Bank Tie for No. 1 in Keynova Group's Q4 2026 Online Banker Scorecard

WILMINGTON, Del., Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Keynova Group, the principal competitive intelligence source for digital financial services firms, today announced the results of its semi-annual Online Banker Scorecard for Q4 2026. For the second consecutive scorecard, Bank of America and U.S. Bank tie for the No. 1 ranking in Keynova Group's competitive evaluation of the digital experiences offered by 17 leading U.S. retail banks.

Keynova Group Logo

"Banks are enhancing the online experience with more robust debit card controls, faster payment options and expanded accessibility resources for greater control over their finances and better access to essential banking and payment services," said Susan Foulds, managing director of Keynova Group. "As digital capabilities continue to evolve, delivering comprehensive experiences with secure, intuitive and inclusive best practices are increasingly important for meeting customer expectations and strengthening long-term relationships."

Key Findings:

Digital Debit Card Management Controls Improving
Online controls for debit card purchases and spending limits are especially important because transactions result in real-time cash debits from deposit accounts. Nearly three-quarters of Scorecard banks are now offering a debit card management screen and an increasing number are enabling customers to limit debit card transactions. More than one-third of the Scorecard banks provide options to set debit card transaction caps by amount and one-quarter allow account owners to control where and how debit cards are used. To enhance security and help customers manage spending, one-quarter of banks enable users to disable debit purchase types such as online or by phone. Displaying a locked debit card indicator on the authenticated landing summary page improves visibility and is trending as well. Surprisingly, however, less than 20% of banks assessed require multi-factor authentication to unlock a debit card.

Banks Expanding Online Payment Flexibility and Speed
As money movement options for consumer accounts expand, banks are addressing competitive pressures from fintechs and neobanks by offering faster payments and transfers. While Citi and U.S. Bank are the only Scorecard banks that currently enable real-time payments for same-day ACH transfers to retail customers, 65% of banks provide an option to expedite ACH account-to-account transfers for next-day delivery. Online-initiated wire payments are becoming more common with nearly half of banks providing online domestic wire transfers and nearly a third supporting international wire payments. Online payment design, as well as transaction alerts, have also improved to help customers avoid unintended transactions or events, such as lapsed recurring payments. Nearly half of the evaluated banks send an alert when recurring payments expire and/or enable account owners to search transaction history by five or more transaction types. Yet less than 20% of banks display scheduled payments on the account summary page, and only one-quarter of banks notify customers there may be insufficient funds in the account to process the bill payment.

title: Bank of America sees a tech retreat not seen since 2006
detail:
Bank of America sees a tech retreat not seen since 2006
Faizan Farooque, Celine Provini

Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

For many years, one of the simplest ways to accumulate wealth has been to control America's largest tech companies.

Millions of Americans have profited from Big Tech's remarkable expansion, whether through individual stocks, index funds, or 401(k)s.

However, the largest investors on Wall Street are now reconsidering. Bank of America (BAC) reported on Nov. 17 that professional money managers reduced their exposure to technology stocks at the fastest monthly pace since June 2006.

The change is noticeable.

Investors were very excited about technology only a month ago. Many people are now wondering whether businesses are overspending on artificial intelligence.

Additionally, Americans who have never directly bought an AI stock may be affected. The concern is particularly relevant for retirement savers whose funds hold large technology companies such as Nvidia (NVDA), Microsoft (MSFT), and Amazon (AMZN).

But the results of the study point to something more intriguing than a straightforward withdrawal from technology.

The majority of investors are still upbeat about equities. They are becoming pickier about where they invest their money.

Also read: Nvidia faces alarming revenue questions before earnings

Bank of America's 25-point shift raises an AI warning

The most recent fund manager poll from Bank of America shows how rapidly attitudes have shifted.

According to Reuters, the net percentage of investors overweight technology stocks fell from 37% in October to just 12% in November. That is the largest monthly decrease since June 2006, amounting to a 25-percentage-point drop.

Investing more in a sector than a selected benchmark would typically indicate is known as being overweight.

The survey measures the proportion of managers in positions above and below the benchmark. Investors did not sell 25% of their technology assets. Nevertheless, there has been a significant shift.

Bank of America polled 169 investors managing approximately $461 billion in assets.

The fact that Americans will abruptly stop using AI is not the main cause for worry. It's whether tech firms can generate enough revenue to cover the billions they've invested in the technology.

Companies are overinvesting, according to a record 38% of investors polled.

Meanwhile, 52% anticipate that within six months, a significant cloud technology business will declare a decrease in capital expenditures. That compares with just 30% in October, according to Investing.com.

title: JPMorgan Names New CFO: Is Jamie Dimon's Succession Plan Taking Shape?
detail:
JPMorgan Names New CFO: Is Jamie Dimon's Succession Plan Taking Shape?
Swayta Shah
Wed, November 18, 2026 at 5:26 AM MST 3 min read
JPM
BAC

Trading disclosure

JPMorgan JPM has announced that Bregje de Best, currently CFO of its Commercial & Investment Bank (CIB), will succeed Jeremy Barnum as firmwide CFO following first-quarter 2027 reporting. Barnum will become vice chairman and remain with the company until early 2028.

The latest leadership reshuffle comes as JPMorgan continues preparing its management team for the eventual retirement of longtime CEO Jamie Dimon, raising questions about whether the bank's succession strategy is gradually taking shape. De Best, who joined JPMorgan in 2006, has extensive experience across banking, markets and finance and should support financial oversight, capital allocation and strategic decision-making across the bank's diversified operations.

The CFO transition follows several senior management changes aimed at strengthening JPMorgan's leadership pipeline. In January 2025, Jennifer Piepszak was named chief operating officer, succeeding Daniel Pinto, who announced plans to retire by the end of 2026. Further, in June 2026, JPMorgan appointed Doug Petno and Troy Rohrbaugh as co-presidents. Petno assumed sole leadership of CIB, while Rohrbaugh became CEO of Consumer & Community Banking following Marianne Lake's decision to retire.

These moves suggest JPMorgan is positioning experienced executives in critical leadership roles while ensuring management continuity. The staggered transitions also provide executives with opportunities to demonstrate their capabilities across major business divisions.

A stable leadership bench could help sustain investor confidence as Jamie Dimon remains CEO for now. Dimon, the longest-tenured CEO among major U.S. banks, has led the bank for more than two decades and has no immediate plans to step down. Nonetheless, the latest CFO appointment, alongside earlier leadership changes, signals a deliberate effort to build a robust succession framework.

Succession Planning at JPMorgan's Peers

Two close peers of JPM are Bank of America BAC and Citigroup C.

Bank of America has strengthened its succession planning by appointing Dean Athanasia and Jim DeMare as co-presidents in September 2025, while elevating CFO Alastair Borthwick to executive vice president. These moves position experienced executives as potential successors to CEO Brian Moynihan, ensuring leadership continuity and operational stability at Bank of America.

Citigroup has reinforced its leadership pipeline under CEO Jane Fraser through strategic appointments and internal promotions. The March 2026 CFO transition from Mark Mason to Gonzalo Luchetti and subsequent senior management reshuffles reflect efforts to develop experienced executives, ensure operational continuity and support long-term succession readiness at Citigroup.

Clark Howard says savers at big banks like JPM and WFC earn about $1 a year per $10,000, while Treasury I bonds pay roughly $551.

The 5.51% I bond rate combines a 1.4% fixed rate that never changes with an inflation piece that resets every six months.

I bonds lock up cash for a year and forfeit three months of interest before year five, so emergency money belongs in online savings.

Building a portfolio and living off one are two completely different skills, and almost nobody teaches the second. This problem is what The Definitive Guide to Retirement Income helps, and it is free today. Read more here. (Sponsor)

Clark Howard was blunt on his November 16 show. If your savings sit at JPMorgan Chase (NYSE:JPM), Bank of America (NYSE:BAC), Citigroup (NYSE:C) or Wells Fargo (NYSE:WFC), the syndicated consumer money host told listeners, "you hate your money. You absolutely hate your money."

LordRunar / Getty Images

He also gave the reason. "The biggest banks are going to pay you 1/100th of 1% on your savings," he said, while "the US Treasury will pay you 5.51% on your savings."

On $10,000, that works out to about $1 a year versus roughly $551. That gap is what you give up by leaving cash where it sits.

Howard Is Right About the Banks, and Treasury's Numbers Back Him

My conclusion: Howard's attack on big-bank savings rates holds up. His I bond pitch also works, but only for money you can lock away for at least a year. If you put your emergency cash into I bonds, you can't get it back when an emergency hits.

TreasuryDirect confirms a 5.51% rate on I bonds issued from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2027. That rate combines a 1.4% fixed rate with a 2% semiannual inflation rate.

The fixed rate matters most, because Treasury says it never changes. Bonds bought from July through October locked in just 0.9% fixed. Buy today and you lock in 1.4% above inflation for up to 30 years.
